1. Import the CSV (33 × 2: Borough, Energy_value) and the neighbor‐list file into two Python objects using pandas.  
2. Create an undirected adjacency dictionary: key = borough, value = list of geographic neighbors. Validate that every borough in the energy table appears in the adjacency list and vice-versa; raise an error if not.  
3. For every borough i, calculate N̄_i = mean(Energy_value of its neighbors). (If any neighbor’s Energy_value were missing we would exclude that neighbor from the mean; if all neighbors were missing we would drop borough i from all subsequent analysis. In our data set Energy_value has 0 missing values, so no exclusions will occur.)  
4. Build a pandas DataFrame with two numeric columns:  
   • X = N̄_i (neighbor mean)  
   • Y = E_i  (borough’s own energy value)  
5. ITERATIVE-R procedure to eliminate masking bias:  
   a. Fit an ordinary least-squares model Y = β₀ + β₁X on the full 33-row table.  
   b. Compute studentized (externally standardized) residuals r_i = e_i / (s√(1-h_ii)), where e_i is the raw residual, h_ii is leverage, and s is the RMSE of the current model.  
   c. Flag any borough with |r_i| > 2.5 as a provisional spatial outlier.  
   d. If at least one new borough is flagged (excluding those already removed), temporarily remove ALL flagged boroughs except Bromley (we must still decide about it) from the data set, refit the OLS model on the reduced table, and repeat steps b–d.  
   e. Iterate until no new boroughs (other than Bromley) meet the |r_i| > 2.5 rule. This converged model is the final “uncontaminated” citywide relationship.  
6. Using the final model from Step 5, compute Bromley’s studentized residual r_Bromley:  
   • Predict Ŷ_Bromley from the model.  
   • Residual e_B = Y_Bromley − Ŷ_Bromley.  
   • Studentize e_B with the RMSE and leverage values from the final model (Bromley was not part of the fitting sample if it had been flagged during iteration; leverage is then computed as x_B·(XᵀX)^−1·x_Bᵀ using the final design matrix).  
7. Decision rule for Bromley:  
   • If |r_Bromley| ≤ 2.5  → NOT AN OUTLIER.  
   • If r_Bromley >  2.5      → OUTLIER - HIGH.  
   • If r_Bromley < −2.5      → OUTLIER - LOW.  
8. Report Bromley’s final studentized residual (real number from Step 6) in the required one-line format.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
energy_path = "chunks_csv/outlierr/2022_energy.csv"
adj_path    = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df_energy = pd.read_csv(energy_path)          # columns: borough, Energy_value
df_adj    = pd.read_csv(adj_path)             # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build undirected adjacency dictionary
adj_dict = {b: set() for b in df_energy["borough"].unique()}

for _, row in df_adj.iterrows():
    b1, b2 = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    # Add only if both boroughs are known (they are, by data description)
    adj_dict.setdefault(b1, set()).add(b2)
    adj_dict.setdefault(b2, set()).add(b1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute neighbour mean energy for each borough
energy_series = df_energy.set_index("borough")["Energy_value"]

neighbor_mean = {}
for b, neighs in adj_dict.items():
    # Mean over the neighbours' Energy_value
    neigh_vals = energy_series.reindex(list(neighs)).dropna()
    if len(neigh_vals) == 0:
        continue           # would drop the borough, but this never happens here
    neighbor_mean[b] = neigh_vals.mean()

# Create DataFrame with own value (Y) and neighbour mean (X)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "borough": list(neighbor_mean.keys()),
    "Y": [energy_series[b] for b in neighbor_mean.keys()],
    "X": [neighbor_mean[b] for b in neighbor_mean.keys()]
})

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. ITERATIVE-R procedure to mitigate masking
removed = set()                 # boroughs removed as outliers (not Bromley)
BROMLEY = "Bromley"

while True:
    # Data currently used for fitting (Bromley must stay even if it is an outlier)
    fit_df = df[~df["borough"].isin(removed)].copy()

    # --- OLS: Y = beta0 + beta1*X
    X_mat = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(fit_df)), fit_df["X"].to_numpy()))
    y     = fit_df["Y"].to_numpy()
    beta  = np.linalg.inv(X_mat.T @ X_mat) @ (X_mat.T @ y)
    y_hat = X_mat @ beta
    resid = y - y_hat

    n, p = X_mat.shape
    s2   = (resid @ resid) / (n - p)
    s    = np.sqrt(s2)
    # leverages
    H    = X_mat @ np.linalg.inv(X_mat.T @ X_mat) @ X_mat.T
    h    = np.diag(H)

    stud_resid = resid / (s * np.sqrt(1 - h))

    fit_df["stud_resid"] = stud_resid

    # Identify provisional outliers (|r|>2.5) except Bromley
    mask_new = (fit_df["borough"] != BROMLEY) & (fit_df["stud_resid"].abs() > 2.5)
    new_outliers = set(fit_df.loc[mask_new, "borough"])

    if not new_outliers.difference(removed):
        # no NEW outliers found, stop iterating
        final_df = fit_df.copy()
        final_beta = beta
        final_h    = h
        final_s    = s
        break
    # else: add them and iterate again
    removed.update(new_outliers)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compute Bromley's studentized residual in the final model
bromley_idx = final_df.index[final_df["borough"] == BROMLEY][0]

e_b  = final_df.loc[bromley_idx, "stud_resid"]  # already studentized

z_B = float(e_b)   # ensure plain Python float

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Decision rule
if abs(z_B) <= 2.5:
    verdict = "NOT AN OUTLIER"
elif z_B > 2.5:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - HIGH"
else:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - LOW"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Reporting
data_points_used = len(final_df)

print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (z = {z_B})")
